notes: §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR1: "A SORT statement may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion." SortBinder.SortBindFile calls ScreenDeclarativePlacement, which refuses a file SORT (COBOL2700) whenever EnclosingContext.InDeclarative holds: a USE section found by BinderContext.DeclarativeAtCursor or, since kb/Work PB5275, a USE FOR DEBUGGING section (ProcedureTableBuilder.InDebuggingSection); since kb/Work PB5274 VersionConformancePass.GateSortMergeProcedures asks the lexical ban on a SORT written in an input or output procedure only from 2023, so the 1985 'anywhere' holds there. Probes at --std 85 (work-rs-02/c5): (b) SORT nested two IFs deep in a USE AFTER EXCEPTION section and SORT (and MERGE) in a USE FOR DEBUGGING section: COBOL2700; accepted and run: SORT nested in IF inside an inline PERFORM in a main section ('AAA', 'BBB', 'CCC'), SORT and MERGE written (unexecuted) in an input and an output procedure ('R BBB', 'DONE'; COBOL2700/COBOL1572 at --std 2023); (c) a table SORT (2002 Format 2): COBOL0870; (e) sequential USING/GIVING. Classes a, d and f do not reach a placement rule. Witness: a SORT in a USE AFTER ERROR section, refused. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read DIVERGES, naming kb/Work PB1139 (landed), kb/Work PB5274 (landed), kb/Work PB5275 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5274 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "A SORT statement may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion."; 2023: "shall not appear in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, in an input or output procedure, or in a". Both bar SORT in declaratives. Judged on this rule's text alone, 2023 also bars SORT in input or output procedures, which the 1985 'anywhere' wording allowed.
